Appgotchi signs in with an App Store Connect API key. Do you already have one?
Add your .p8 file and Issuer ID on one screen.
Three short steps, about two minutes.
Add your App Store Connect key
App Store Connect lets you download each key only once, so keep the file somewhere safe.
Open Users and Access, then Integrations, then Team Keys.
Generate a key named “Appgotchi” with the App Manager role.
Appgotchi will need it for releases later. Creating keys needs Admin or Account Holder access.
Appgotchi uses it to open the right Play Console pages for you.
Copy the Account ID under your developer name.
Appgotchi reads your apps and reports through two of Google’s APIs.
In Google Cloud Console, create a project or choose one you have.
Enable the Google Play Developer Reporting API.
Enable the Google Play Android Developer API.
Used later for releases and reviews.
This is the account Appgotchi signs in as. It needs no Cloud roles.
Create a service account named “appgotchi-readonly”, then choose Done.
Open it and go to the Keys tab.
Choose Add key, then Create new key, then JSON. Google offers the file only once.
Google Cloud organizations created since May 2024 block service account keys by default. Ask an organization admin to allow keys for this project, or use a project outside your organization.
Don’t commit this file to a code repository.
Give the service account read-only access. You can add more later without a new key.
Open Users and permissions and choose Invite new users.
Under Account permissions, tick “View app information and download bulk reports (read-only)”, then choose Invite user.
Reviews, releases and revenue will ask for more permissions when you turn them on.
Google can take a while to apply new permissions. Only apps you’ve uploaded to Play Console appear.
